title: Harden native MCP post-selection contracts

requirement.summary: Make Alignment Resolve and current-Agent self-review reject repairable normalized input with precise privacy-safe diagnostics while preserving atomic retry.

objective.rationale: The installed Adapter reaches the human selection boundary, but the native post-selection input boundary has only happy-path fixture evidence.

goal: Add strict Adapter-owned validation and fixture coverage for Resolve, self-review start, and self-review completion so repairable failures are classified and atomic before another live replay.
non_goals: Do not run another external replay.
Do not add a host, model, credential, network call, consumer change, release, publication, or deployment.
Do not claim semantic correctness or complete live-journey evidence.
acceptance_signals: Repairable Resolve and self-review input failures return bounded field, rule, stage, and retryability metadata without rejected values.
Rejected post-selection calls do not advance alignment or self-review state and a corrected retry succeeds in the same process.
Codex and Claude fixtures retain the same resolved advisory self-review path with zero AgentGov model or network calls.
Documentation distinguishes deterministic contract parity from unproven live host behavior.

items: Over-broad diagnostics could expose normalized content or misclassify internal failures.
Validation after state mutation could break same-process retry.

stop_conditions: Stop if the change requires weakening Core, retaining raw conversation or source content, or expanding project authority.
Stop if a rejected call advances journey state or internal exception text would be returned.

decision.rationale: The product owner selected the recommended post-selection contract slice on 2026-08-07.
